revision_reason: Change cr-0001 placed standard-input support into the current stage as task tk-002 and added requirement r-0004.

phases.title: First working path
phases.outcome: The line counter counts non-empty lines in a named file, offers machine-readable output, and reads standard input when no path is given.

stages.title: Line counter features
stages.outcome: The command gains a --json flag and standard-input support, with tests for both.

tasks.title: Add a --json flag that prints the result as a JSON object
tasks.scope: Add a --json flag to linecount.js that prints the count as a JSON object instead of the plain number, and add tests for the flag in linecount.test.js. Do not change how lines are counted and do not add dependencies.
tasks.output: linecount.js accepts --json and prints a JSON object with the count; tests cover the flag.
acceptance: Running node linecount.js --json with a file path prints a JSON object with a count property and exits with code 0.
Running without the flag still prints the plain number.

tasks.title: Read from standard input when no path is given
tasks.scope: Change linecount.js to read and count standard input when no path argument is given, keeping the current behavior for a named file, and add tests that pipe input in linecount.test.js. Do not add dependencies.
tasks.output: linecount.js counts standard input when no path is given; tests cover piped input.
acceptance: Piping text into node linecount.js with no path prints the count of non-empty lines and exits with code 0.
Running with a file path behaves as before.

requirements.text: The command prints the number of non-empty lines in the named file.
A final line without a trailing newline is still counted.
The --json flag prints a JSON object with the count.
When no path is given, the command reads standard input.

changes.summary: Read from standard input when no path is given.
changes.reason: The user asked for pipeline use after accepting the plan.
